name: Alma Harmony XL

lead: Alma Harmony XL (and the Harmony XL Pro) is a multi-application aesthetic laser platform used in clinics. It helps improve how skin looks by treating pigmentation, redness and visible vessels, wrinkles and texture, acne and acne scars, and by removing unwanted hair, depending on which applicator is attached.

Published studies on its applicators include small clinical trials of its fractional Q-switched 1,064 nm laser on photoaged skin, a retrospective multicentre study of IPL for rosacea, and a trial of a 1,540 nm Er:Glass laser for acne and scars.

paras: Treatment is given in a clinic over a course of sessions spaced a few weeks apart, with different applicators chosen for vascular, pigmented, resurfacing or acne concerns. Downtime varies by applicator.

As with other clinic lasers, treatment is delivered by trained providers and outcomes depend on skin type, settings and the condition treated. Studies of the platform report low rates of significant adverse effects, though some are small.

angle.text: The platform is used in clinics to even out colour, reduce visible vessels and refine texture. Different handpieces cover different concerns.

lead: Alma Harmony XL Pro is a multi-application aesthetic laser platform for clinics, expandable with applicators for skin resurfacing, remodeling, vascular and pigmented lesions, tattoos, acne and scars, and hair removal. [1]

Core technologies include Q-switched Nd:YAG, a Pixel Q-switch for non-ablative fractional treatment, a roller attachment, and Alma's AFT intense pulsed light. Applicators include ClearLift, ClearSkin Pro (1540 nm Er:Glass), iPixel (2940 nm Er:YAG), LP Nd:YAG and IPL handpieces. [1]
Published clinical work on the platform covers photoaging, rosacea, acne and scars, and vascular lesions. [2][3][4][5][6]
infobox: Q-switch Nd:YAG, Pixel Q-switch, Er:Glass, Er:YAG, IPL

paras: The platform lists ClearLift (Q-switched Nd:YAG for pigmentation, tattoos and rejuvenation), ClearSkin Pro (1540 nm for active acne and scars), iPixel (2940 nm Er:YAG for resurfacing), LP Nd:YAG (vascular lesions), Dye-VL/Dye-SR and VL/PL 540 Cooled IPL handpieces, Speed AFT for hair removal and NIR Face for collagen-stimulating heating. [1]

A 2014 clinical trial of the fractional Q-switched 1,064 nm laser in 10 women with photodamage found that 60% had at least one-point Glogau improvement at 3 months. [2] A 2020 study in 16 women using the ClearLift Q-switched laser reported a 30-40% mean reduction in aging signs on a global scale by blinded experts with no significant adverse effects. [3]

A 2025 multicentre retrospective study of 82 rosacea patients treated with the VL/PL Cooled applicator reported over 75% clearance in 69.5%. [4] A 2018 study of 22 acne patients using the 1540 nm laser assessed acne lesions and scars. [5] A 2023 review concluded the LP1064 applicator is safe and effective for vein and vascular lesions. [6]
